title: Group Chat and Mixtape
premise: Coral Halloran, seventeen, has spent years holding her family together while her mother works hospital night shifts, and she's built her entire college essay around being 'fine.' But when her AP English class is assigned a brutally honest prompt—'What are you not saying?'—her answer, and her classmates' answers, accidentally surface evidence that the school board covered up toxic mold in the building that made her little sister sick. As the district moves to silence the students and Coral's carefully managed invisibility unravels, she must choose between protecting the fragile peace at home and burning it all down with the truth. In the end, the kids publish the mixtape of testimony they've been compiling, the board resigns, and Coral finally writes an essay that tells the truth: she was never fine, and that's the strongest thing about her.
about_author: Ada Thackeray is a former high school English teacher who spent a decade collecting the things students wrote and never turned in. She writes from a drafty attic in coastal Maine, where she still keeps every mixtape anyone ever made her.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A morning in the Halloran household: burnt toast, a missing permission slip, seven-year-old Junie's cough, and Coral orchestrating it all before catching the bus. She's perfected the art of looking fine. Emotional beat: loving exhaustion, the mask going on.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. New AP English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns an ungraded essay: 'What are you not saying?' The class goes silent. Coral writes three safe sentences, then, at 2 a.m., writes the real thing—and can't delete it. Emotional beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Group Chat Rules
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet the group chat—'the basement kids': Theo, Priya, Marcus, and Dez, the lunch-table misfits who've become her found family. They trade secrets like currency, all under an unspoken rule: nothing leaves the chat. Emotional beat: belonging with conditions.

chapters.title: Junie's Fever
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Junie's cough turns into a 103-degree fever and a night in the ER. The doctor asks questions about the school building that make Coral's stomach drop. Mom misses it all, working a double. Emotional beat: fear, and the first suspicion something is wrong.

chapters.title: What Priya Found in the Ceiling
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, the AV-club archivist, mentions black streaks above the gym ceiling tiles and a maintenance log she photographed 'for fun.' Coral connects it to Junie. The chat debates. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Essay That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Ms. Okafor returns the essays, but Coral's honest draft is missing from the stack—and so are three others. Someone read them. Someone kept them. Emotional beat: violation, paranoia, the mask slipping in public.

chapters.title: Board Meeting, Public Comment, Three Minutes
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, debate-team loyalist and school-board-obsessed, drags the group to a public meeting where a parent's mold complaint is buried in thirty seconds. Coral almost speaks and doesn't. Emotional beat: the cost of silence, witnessed.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price Tag
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, whose dad works in district maintenance, is warned at home: stay out of it. He tells Coral nothing, and the chat starts to splinter. Emotional beat: the ache of choosing between family and friends.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Idea
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez, who records everything, proposes the mixtape: not a leak, but a compilation—voices, testimony, the story told by the kids who breathe that air. Coral resists; she has siblings to protect. Emotional beat: art as a weapon you're scared to pick up.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Mom, hollowed out by night shifts, catches Coral mid-investigation and forbids it: 'We can't afford this fight.' Coral, who has raised the younger ones, hears the reversal and rages. Emotional beat: the eldest child's resentment finally spoken.

chapters.title: Records Request, Deny, Repeat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya files a public records request; the district stalls, then returns heavily redacted pages. But the redactions themselves are a map. The chat realizes the cover-up is organized. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being right.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father is reassigned after refusing to falsify an inspection report. Theo finally tells the chat everything—and brings his dad's hidden photos. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into courage; the family fractures and heals.

chapters.title: The Prompt Goes Viral
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Ms. Okafor assigns the essay prompt again school-wide. Hundreds of honest answers flood in, and the missing-essay theft becomes a story students tell each other. The group chat becomes a movement overnight. Emotional beat: private pain becomes collective power.

chapters.title: What Coral Isn't Saying
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A quiet chapter: Coral reads Junie a bedtime story, checks the ER bill, and admits to herself she's terrified—not of the board, but of what happens to her family if she stops being 'fine.' Emotional beat: the midpoint reckoning with herself.

chapters.title: The Threat
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. An anonymous letter warns Coral's scholarship recommendation is 'under review'; Dez's locker is vandalized; Priya's camera goes missing. The board is fighting dirty. Emotional beat: intimidation, and the group deciding to be unafraid anyway.

chapters.title: Ms. Okafor's Desk
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confronts Ms. Okafor about the stolen essays. Okafor admits she kept them to protect students from a district that retaliates—and gives Coral the one thing she needs: the name of the contractor who falsified the inspection. Emotional beat: an adult finally on their side.

chapters.title: Side A: Everyone Who Got Sick
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The group records the mixtape's first half: Junie's wheezing, a custodian's anonymous testimony, Theo's dad's voice, student essays read aloud. It's raw and undeniable. Emotional beat: grief assembled into evidence.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The plan: play the mixtape and release the documents at the spring showcase, where every parent and two local reporters will be in the auditorium. Mom, having read Junie's hospital records, shows up and says, 'Do it.' Emotional beat: the family united at last.

chapters.title: Showcase
chapters.summary: Multiple short POV shifts. The mixtape plays over the auditorium speakers; the lights come up on students holding copies of the unredacted records. The board president storms out as reporters' recorders click on. Emotional beat: the climax—truth at maximum volume.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The aftermath: an emergency board session, resignations, an independent inspection confirming black mold, and the school closed for remediation. Some friendships bend; the chat holds. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won vindication.

chapters.title: What Coral Is Saying
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral rewrites her college essay from scratch: not the polished 'fine' version, but the true one—about holding a family together, about the question nobody could stop answering. She hits submit. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, the mask retired.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue-style. Summer: the school reopens clean, Junie breathes easy, Mom switches to day shifts, and Dez burns the group a final mixtape—Side B, all the songs they survived to. Coral presses play with her found family on the hood of Theo's car. Emotional beat: joy, forward motion, home.
